faq.a: They succeed 70 to 80 percent of the time on tasks that take humans less than one hour, and less than 20 percent of the time on tasks that take humans more than 4 hours.
faq.q: How do current AI agents perform on HCAST?

how: Tasks are drawn from machine learning engineering, cybersecurity, software engineering, and general reasoning. Human baselines were collected from 563 skilled people working under identical conditions as AI agents, totaling over 1500 hours, to estimate per task human completion times. AI agents are evaluated by their success rate on each task.
name: HCAST
note: Current frontier AI agents succeed 70 to 80 percent of the time on tasks that take humans less than one hour, but less than 20 percent of the time on tasks that take humans more than 4 hours.

measures: HCAST measures the success rates of AI agents on 189 tasks in machine learning engineering, cybersecurity, software engineering, and general reasoning. It calibrates these tasks by how long they take skilled humans, from one minute to 8 or more hours. This provides a grounded metric connecting AI performance to real world effects.
not_measured: The page text does not state what HCAST does not measure. It focuses on task success rates and human time calibration, and does not describe performance on tasks outside the four listed domains.
interpretation: A published result should be read as the agent's success rate on tasks grouped by how long they take skilled humans. This helps answer whether an agent can be trusted to complete a task that would take a human a given number of hours.
